newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Whitbread pleased with 97 start.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Whitbread pleased with 97 start.

text.p: Brewer-to-leisure group Whitbread Plc is "quite pleased" with the first two months of trading so far this year although the consumer is still very value conscious, chief executive David Thomas said on Wednesday.

"We are quite pleased with the first two months. We have seen a strong build up of consumer confidence over the last year, but the consumer is still very well aware of value," Thomas told Reuters in an interview.

Earlier, Whibtread reported a 12 percent increase in pretax, pre-exceptional profits to 316.5 million stg. Thomas said the company was "reasonably confident" that the introduction of a national minimum wage, a manifesto pledge of the newly-elected Labour party, would not affect Whitbread's business.

The company employs some 80,000 people and a large number of unskilled young bar staff. "It is very much dependent on how it (minimum wage) is set," he said, "We are pretty confident of a good dialogue with politicians going forward."
The company would like to see incentive schemes and training costs taken into account as well as regional variations in standards of living.
"The consumer is not really unnerved at this stage and everything we have heard so far from the Labour party implies consumer confidence will remain high."
He pointed to Whitbread's advance hotel bookings, up two to three percent on the same time last year.
The company plans to sell off underperforming assets in the coming year, to raise some 100 million stg as a minimum target, said Thomas.
This will ensure that its retail estate remains fresh and allows it to re-invest more heavily in contemporary sites and strongly branded areas, he said.
In the coming year Whitbread plans to open a further 250 outlets at a cost of about 400 million stg, up from about 140 and 300 million respectively last year, said Thomas.

The company will develop about 80 Whitbread Inns, turning them into Hogs Head or Brewers Fayre pubs, and open 40 Travel Inns, 45 more Pizza Hut's, 35 Costa Coffee's and 40 Pelican restaurants -- mainly Cafe Rouge or Cafe Dome -- outlets.
